prompts: Remember the little archery games of the Windows 95 days? We want the first level of one, our own, in {WS}/game/index.html, a single file. An archer you aim with the mouse, pulling the bow back for power, balloons to pop, a score on screen, a way to start and a way to lose. How it looks, plays and sounds is your call, and that is what we care about most: a minute of play should be fun, and every shot and hit should feel and sound good. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts, and by playing it.

The game is done and verified; the remaining tabs are pre-existing about:blank and 127.0.0.1 tabs I did not open, so I'll leave them and finish.

[goal] A Win95-style archery balloon-pop level in `game/index.html`, single file, no build step.

[action] Wrote the game (canvas + WebAudio, no assets), opened it in the browser, and played it. Two fixes from live testing: the menu overlay was darkening the sky (lightened `.55`→`.35`), and arrow gravity was too strong to hit balloons (260→90).

[result] Verified by playing:
- Menu renders with title, instructions, "CLICK OR PRESS SPACE" (screenshot).
- Click starts the game; HUD shows SCORE, POPS 0/15, TIME 20 (screenshot).
- Aiming with the mouse, holding draws the bow and fills a POWER bar; release fires an arrow (screenshots).
- A hit popped a balloon: SCORE 20, POPS 1/15, and a "+20" floatie appeared (screenshot).
- Sounds: WebAudio synth for draw, shoot, pop, miss, tick, win, lose (no external files, so they work offline).

How it works: mouse aims; hold to draw (power scales 420–1060); release to shoot. Pop 15 balloons in 20 s to win; timer hitting 0 = lose. Big balloons = 50 pts, small = 20.

[assumptions] "A way to lose" = a 20 s timer; "start" = click/Space from the menu; balloons rise from the ground and sway; 15 pops = level clear (win screen).

[how I know it's right] I opened the file in a real browser and played it: the pop incremented score/pops and spawned the floatie, the power bar and bow-draw responded to holding, and the HUD updated. The one bug I hit (dark sky) was traced to the menu overlay, not the sky, by hooking `fillRect` and confirming `drawSky` fills `#7ec8e3`.

[limits] I did not play a full 20 s to the win/lose screens, but the end-state logic is the same `endGame()` path the pop/timer use, and the menu/lose/win screens share the verified `drawCenter`. Browser tabs I opened are closed; the remaining about:blank/127.0.0.1 tabs pre-date my session.
